{"name":"dev","commit":{"sha":"2e8cacbe1ed4ed0fc31d5b59b9895c811ac0e003","node_id":"C_kwDOAHYhoNoAKDJlOGNhY2JlMWVkNGVkMGZjMzFkNWI1OWI5ODk1YzgxMWFjMGUwMDM","commit":{"author":{"name":"Mat Groves","email":"mat@goodboydigital.com","date":"2026-10-27T09:22:32Z"},"committer":{"name":"GitHub","email":"noreply@github.com","date":"2026-10-27T09:22:32Z"},"message":"fix: upload WebGL2 index buffers through COPY_WRITE_BUFFER; land WebGL1 ranged updates (#12342)

* fix: upload WebGL2 index buffers through COPY_WRITE_BUFFER

An index buffer bound to ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER becomes the index buffer of
whichever vertex array is bound, so uploading one at update() time could
rewrite another geometry's indices. Unbinding and rebinding the vertex array
around the upload avoided that at the cost of two state changes per update.

WebGL2 now uploads index updates through COPY_WRITE_BUFFER, which no vertex
array reads, so the upload changes no draw state. WebGL1 has no copy target:
it unbinds the bound vertex array and lets the next geometry.bind() bind its
own. A buffer that has never been uploaded waits for its first bind, which
binds it to ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER and so makes WebGL2 type it as index data.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: land ranged buffer updates past offset 0 on WebGL1

WebGL1's bufferSubData has no source offset or length, so the WebGL2 form
uploaded the whole array at the update's offset: right at offset 0, and
dropped as out of range anywhere else. WebGL1 now uploads a view of just the
updated elements. This also makes a cacheAsTexture container's ranged vertex
upload land on WebGL1.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
